previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, and pulmonary hypertension was admitted due to a painful, pulsatile mass in the right groin. Imaging confirmed a 4 cm pseudoaneurysm in the right external iliac artery, which had increased in size and required intervention. She underwent placement of a Viabahn stent via percutaneous approach, which successfully excluded the aneurysm. Warfarin was held pre-procedure and resumed afterward, along with initiation of aspirin for stent protection. She received bedside hemodialysis during her stay and was managed for post-procedural pain and constipation. Physical therapy confirmed she was ambulating independently. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor the puncture site, avoid heavy lifting, and continue all home medications including anticoagulation.
